text:
maria.reyes: Heads-up: during the Rerank rollout we saw 3 orgs get a flurry of 429s. Burst budget drained in ~18s for those orgs. Repro on staging with similar traffic. Anyone free to brainstorm short vs steady-state tuning?

dave: saw it too. spike was mostly short-lived bursts from a partner integration hitting /v1/completions concurrently. Our token bucket config (per-org) had burst_capacity=100, refill_rate=5/s.

anita: that matches. Seems the leaky-bucket model on the aggregator is stricter (leak config) — we leak at 3/s to downstream pools causing imbalance.

ken-h: thinking aloud — three knobs: burst_capacity, refill_rate, and warmup. For short spikes we want larger burst_capacity; for steady-state we want correct refill_rate to avoid sustained 429s.

sam-sre: telemetry shows buckets hit 0. Query I used: ```promql
min_over_time(token_bucket_available{env="prod"}[1m])
``` Also dashboard panels: bucket_fill_ratio and recent_refills. We should add an alert when bucket_fill_ratio < 0.1 for >30s.

maria.reyes: good. Question: should burst be per-org OR per-key? Current behavior: per-org global bucket then per-api-key soft limits.

dave: per-org is safer for preventing a single key from exhausting org budget. But it means noisy neighbor inside org. Maybe hierarchical: per-org + per-key with borrowing semantics.

anita: propose config example: ```json
{
  "policy": "hierarchical",
  "org": {"burst":200,"rate":10},
  "key": {"burst":50,"rate":5},
  "borrow_from_org": true
}
```

ken-h: debate: enforce at edge (ingress LB) vs at aggregator. Edge gives early 429s and saves compute, but we lose KV cache locality. Aggregator enforcement lets us observe and route to fallback model.

sam-sre: Ops prefer edge because it reduces wasted work. Maybe hybrid: pre-check at edge for quick 429, then aggregator does final check allowing queued requests with token reservation.

rate-limiter-bot: deploy 2024-05-25T15:05: applied ephemeral_queue feature toggle to canary orgs.

maria.reyes: UX question — in Console, we should show 'burst budget' timeline and predicted depletion if current rate continues. Also allow admins to temporarily increase burst for N minutes.

dave: agree. Add UI controls: 'grant temporary burst +X for T minutes' + audit log. Also show real-time consumption per key.

anita: for rollout, canary with 3 orgs, monitor new metrics and keep default lower for new signups (protect backend).

ken-h: action items: 1) add dashboard panels + alerts (sam). 2) implement hierarchical borrowing logic (eng). 3) Console UI mockups (maria). 4) decide edge vs aggregator hybrid plan (dave/ken).

maria.reyes: I'll add to roadmap and schedule sync. ping @dave @sam-sre for a 30-min call tomorrow. :calendar:
